tasks.subject: statsutils: finish Pearson zero-denominator review and regression coverage
tasks.body:
Follow the maintainer review on #434: c0 == 0 selects Type I for negative c2, otherwise Type VI. Existing Normal and Gamma branches retain precedence. Note that rounded precision widens the Type V boundary.

Delete the dead random _test_pearson helper and replace broad type-membership assertions with concrete Type IV, V, and VI samples. Add exact-moment boundary coverage that fails with ZeroDivisionError before this fix and passes afterward.

tasks.subject: setutils, listutils: streamline bulk removal and fix list bounds (#440)
tasks.body:
difference_update/intersection_update looped discard() per item; every
384 scattered removals that triggers a full O(n) _compact, making bulk
removal O(n*k/384). Rebuild once in O(n) when the removal count exceeds
the compaction threshold. Fixes #{{ISSUE_NUMBER}}

tasks.subject: mathutils: resolve negative Bits indices (#450)
tasks.body:
__getitem__ only bounds-checked k >= self.len, so a negative index put
the mask above the top of the stored value and the AND always came out
0: Bits('1011')[-1] returned False when the last bit is 1, and
out-of-range negatives returned False rather than raising. Negative
slices were already correct, since that branch goes through as_bin().

Adjust and bounds-check negative indices the way
IndexedSet._get_real_index does (d0a284f).

tasks.subject: dictutils: preserve iterator values in addlist (#458)
tasks.body:
addlist() traverses its argument twice: once to insert the keys into the
linked list, once to extend the backing values list. A one-shot iterator
is exhausted by the first pass, so the second added nothing and the OMD
was left internally inconsistent - keys() and repr() showed the values
while getlist() returned [] and get() raised IndexError.

An empty iterator was worse: the `if not v` guard is truthy for an
exhausted generator, so the key was recorded with no values and len()
disagreed with keys().

Materialize the argument once, before the guard. The docstring already
promises that "tuples and other sequences and iterables work"; the
doctest uses range(), which is re-iterable, which is why this went
unnoticed. urlutils carries a vendored copy of the method with the same
defect, so it gets the same fix.

tasks.subject: statsutils: add mode() for most-common value, incl. categorical data (#453)
tasks.body:
The mean and median were available as Stats attributes and module-level
helpers, but there was no mode. Add it as a _StatsProperty so it also
gets a module-level convenience function, using collections.Counter so
non-numeric, categorical data is supported. Ties resolve to the value
seen first in the data, matching statistics.mode.

Closes #90

Co-authored-by: Chris (ChrisJr404) <11917633+ChrisJr404@users.noreply.github.com>

tasks.subject: strutils: add ellipsize for word-boundary-aware truncation
tasks.body:
Truncates to max_len (ellipsis included), cutting at the last space
so words are never broken, stripping trailing whitespace and sentence
punctuation at the cut. A period between two digits is treated as a
decimal point, not sentence punctuation, so numbers like 6.5% stay
whole. Single tokens longer than max_len are hard-cut at the limit;
max_len must exceed len(ellipsis) or ValueError is raised.

Includes doctests, tests (boundary no-op, space cut, decimal
preservation, hard cut, custom ellipsis, max_len sweep, ValueError),
and a changelog entry under unreleased 26.1.1.

tasks.subject: Fix issupserset typo in _ComplementSet comparisons (#438)
tasks.body:
_ComplementSet.__le__ (- - branch) and __ge__ (+ + branch) called
set.issupserset, which does not exist, raising AttributeError whenever
those paths were hit. Correct the spelling to issuperset, matching the
issubset/issuperset used in the sibling branches and the class's own
issuperset method.

Co-authored-by: uttam12331 <uttam12331@users.noreply.github.com>

tasks.subject: funcutils: forward target-keyword-only args as keywords in wraps invocations (#445)
tasks.body:
wraps(g)(f) generates a shim with g's signature that calls f. When f
declares a parameter keyword-only that g accepts positionally, the
generated invocation passed it positionally and f raised TypeError
(#261). The defaulted flavor of this was fixed as a side effect of
the #343 keyword-forwarding work; the non-defaulted flavor (donor arg
positional and undefaulted) and the varargs flavor still broke.

get_invocation_str() now takes an optional 'target' -- the callable
the generated invocation will call -- and forwards any arg that
target only accepts as a keyword as name=name, overriding the
positional rules (including the varargs one: _call(a, *va, b=b) binds
correctly precisely because a target-kw-only name can never collide
with target's positionals). update_wrapper passes wrapper as the
target. Targets without introspectable signatures (some C callables)
fall back to signature-based forwarding alone.

Fixes #261

tasks.subject: Fix off-by-one in Bits length check
tasks.body:
The largest value representable in len_ bits is 2 ** len_ - 1, but the
guard used 'val > 2 ** len_', so Bits(4, 2) was accepted and produced a
3-bit value ('100') with a declared len of 2, silently breaking the
len/__getitem__ invariant and failing to round-trip. Use '>=' so a value
needing more than len_ bits raises, matching the guard's error message.
The auto-computed len_ branch never trips the stricter check.

tasks.subject: iterutils: unify xfrange with frange's count-based semantics
tasks.body:
xfrange's accumulate-and-compare loop ('while cur < stop') assumed
ascending iteration: negative steps toward a lower stop yielded
nothing, and it disagreed with frange on element counts at inexact
float boundaries (xfrange-style accumulation produced 11 elements for
stop=1.0/step=0.1 where frange's up-front ceil((stop - start) / step)
count gives 10 -- the doctests never caught it because they only use
exactly-representable fractions).

xfrange now computes the same up-front count as frange and yields the
accumulated values: descending ranges work, wrong-direction ranges are
empty like range(1, 5, -1), counts always match frange, and the
step=0 ValueError is preserved. frange itself is byte-for-byte
unchanged; its output is the compat contract.
